motion.name: ease

motion.name: goat-wiggle
motion.purpose: Hover on the die-cut goat; held still under reduced motion.

motion.name: peek-rise
motion.purpose: The mascot rises a little when its slot or speaker card is hovered or focused; reduced motion keeps it still.

motion.name: goat-pop
motion.value: 640ms, from translateY(108%) through a stretch, an overshoot and a squash to rest
motion.purpose: The companion goat rising out from behind a slot's edge.

motion.name: goat-duck
motion.value: 420ms, a small lift then translateY(108%) behind the edge
motion.purpose: The companion goat hiding, also when the pointer comes within 110px.

motion.name: goat-hop
motion.value: 620 to 900ms, an arc with a crouch, a take-off stretch and a landing squash
motion.purpose: The companion goat moving to the next slot, its painted head turned towards where it goes.

motion.name: goat-turn
motion.value: 300ms, the painted head swapped at the top of a small lift and squash
motion.purpose: The companion goat looking left and right with its own turned head; never a mirrored picture.

narrative.overview:
GoatConf is a sticker album opened flat on an album-blue ground. The organiser sticks in the core facts as matte die-cut stickers; every other numbered slot is printed empty on the white page and waits for whoever brings a talk, a workshop or a walk. The album is the whole site: a blue ground printed with faint cloven-hoof marks, white album pages with rounded corners, a blue band across the top of each page inside a thin white edge, a numbered sequence that runs through the whole album, a night-blue "shiny" page for the goat story, and a night-blue back cover.

The material is printed paper and vinyl, not screen chrome. Stickers have a white die-cut border, a soft lift off the page and a diagonal gloss; empty slots are flat, dashed and printed in the album's own blue at low strength, each with a faint goat silhouette and a printed number. Hierarchy comes from scale contrast in condensed uppercase lettering, not from weight changes or colour noise. The goat itself appears once per spread as a die-cut yellow sticker with a white edge.

The world refuses the dark tech-conference hero with a speaker grid. It also refuses to pretend: what is decided is stuck in, what is undecided stays an empty printed slot, and nothing is announced as a sticker before it is true.
keyCharacteristics: Album-blue ground with a faint hoof-print pattern; white pages float on it with rounded corners and a soft drop.
Two states of every fact: a stuck-in sticker (decided) or an empty printed slot (undecided or open to you).
One numbered sequence across the album, yellow on stickers, printed on slots.
Condensed uppercase Bricolage lettering at strong scale contrast; Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for reading.
Stickers sit still in their slots, tilted, with no entrance animation.

rules.name: The Red Stamp Rule
rules.body: Red appears only as the "Yours?" stamp on an empty slot. It never marks an error, a price, a link or a heading.

rules.name: The Yellow Means Stuck Rule
rules.body: Yellow fills only things that are decided or numbered: a stuck-in number, a fact, the status. An empty slot never carries a yellow fill; its number is printed in blue.

rules.name: The Lettered, Not Typed Rule
rules.body: Every heading, caption, number and stamp is Bricolage at 800, condensed and uppercase. Weight never varies to make hierarchy; size does.

rules.name: The Reading Face Rule
rules.body: Any sentence longer than a label is Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, never the display face.

rules.name: The Printed Is Flat Rule
rules.body: An empty slot, a printed number and the stamp have no shadow. Only things stuck onto the page lift.

rules.name: The Matte Rule
rules.body: Stickers are matte: no sheen, no gradient, so photos keep their true colours and a fact sticker reads as flat printed blue. Their shadows stay short and light, so they sit on the page rather than float above it.

dos: **Do** show a decided fact as a stuck-in sticker and an undecided or open one as an empty printed slot, with its reason in the slot's explanation.
**Do** give every sticker and slot the next number in the album's single sequence.
**Do** keep stickers sticker-sized: two across on phones, never full-width cards.
**Do** set a small per-sticker tilt between -2 and 2 degrees, and vary it between neighbours.
**Do** credit every photo on the page that shows it, in credit type under the stickers.
**Do** write plain sentences: one idea per sentence, common words, and no em dashes anywhere, including captions, alt text and generated pages.
donts: **Don't** use red for anything but the "Yours?" stamp.
**Don't** put a fact on a sticker before it is true: an unconfirmed date stays "June 2027" on the fact sticker and an empty slot for the exact days.
**Don't** give printed things (slots, printed numbers, stamps) a lift, or stuck stickers a dashed outline or a gloss.
**Don't** write self-aware copy about the album, the design or the site itself; the page talks about the conference, Tuzla and the visitor.
**Don't** add small labels above headings, glyph icons, or goat drawings beyond the mark and the mascot; the band, the numbers, the mark and the mascot carry the page.
**Don't** let the goat cover a fact, stand in for text a screen reader needs, or appear on the code of conduct or budget content as a joke.
